title: password storage hashing MFA account recovery and rate limits
concepts: Passwords are low-entropy human secrets, so stored verifiers require deliberately expensive password hashing with a unique salt and configurable work factor. General-purpose fast hashes and reversible encryption are not equivalent.
MFA adds an authenticator but factor and recovery strength matter. Phishing-resistant public-key authenticators provide stronger resistance to phishing than replayable one-time codes.
Enrollment, reset, recovery, throttling, credential-stuffing defenses, session revocation, and notification are part of account security; recovery paths need protections comparable to login.
Sensitive changes should require a current authenticated session and suitable re-authentication. Avoid account-enumeration leaks while keeping legitimate recovery usable.
